hypothesis: Moving the string-body scan of LineIndex.build (src/indexer/lineIndex.ts on 1d2377e) from the top-of-loop `if (inString) { ... continue; }` branch (L258-293) into the `case 0x22:` arm of the outer switch (L304-307), so that an opening quote scans its string body in place (same 4x `> 0x5c` byte reject + same byte tail) and resumes the outer loop right after the closing quote, with a one-time pre-loop carry block that finishes a string straddling the chunk start (consuming the cross-chunk `escaped` byte), will raise the primary speedup from 1.623 to ~1.75-1.80 (~1.10-1.16x relative), because every string currently costs an extra outer-loop round trip (set inString, break, i++, re-test `while (i < n)`, re-test `if (inString)`, re-test `if (escaped)`) and every outside-string byte pays the `if (inString)` test; after the change the outer loop runs only outside strings, so that test disappears from the hot path. This is a control-flow (architecture) change only: the 4x byte reject and the byte tail are kept exactly as they are (no SWAR / Uint32Array word loop, which is planner_a's change), and the WCLS skip, the other switch cases, checkpoint modulo, record pushes, for-await loop, Buffer.from conversion and EOF handling are untouched.

steps.change: Add a one-time chunk-start carry block between `let i = 0;` (L256) and `while (i < n) {` (L257). It runs only when the previous chunk ended inside a string, and reuses the existing loop body verbatim except that the escaped-carry is consumed once up front: `if (inString && n > 0) { if (escaped) { escaped = false; i = 1; /* first byte of this chunk is the escaped byte */ } for (;;) { while (i + 3 < n && buf[i] > 0x5c && buf[i + 1] > 0x5c && buf[i + 2] > 0x5c && buf[i + 3] > 0x5c) i += 4; if (i >= n) break; /* string spans the whole chunk: inString stays true */ const sb = buf[i++]; if (sb > 0x5c) continue; if (sb === 0x22) { inString = false; break; } if (sb === 0x5c) { if (i < n) { i++; } else { escaped = true; break; } } } }`. The `n > 0` guard keeps an empty chunk from consuming `escaped` (the old `while (i < n)` also did nothing for n === 0). For n === 1 with escaped set, i becomes 1, the for(;;) breaks at `i >= n`, escaped is false and inString stays true, which matches the old `escaped = false; i++; continue;` path. When the string closes mid-chunk, the outer while starts at the byte after the closing quote with inString === false, the same state the old `continue` produced.

Delete the whole `if (inString) { ... continue; }` branch at the top of `while (i < n) {` (L258-293: the `if (escaped) { escaped = false; i++; continue; }` block, the `for (;;) { while (i + 3 < n && buf[i] > 0x5c && ... ) i += 4; if (i >= n) break; const sb = buf[i++]; if (sb > 0x5c) continue; if (sb === 0x22 /* " */) { inString = false; break; } if (sb === 0x5c) { if (i < n) { i++; } else { escaped = true; break; } } }` loop and the trailing `continue;`). The while body then starts directly with the existing WCLS skip `if (WCLS[buf[i]] === 0) { lineHasContent = true; do { i++; } while (i < n && WCLS[buf[i]] === 0); if (i >= n) break; }`. Invariant after steps 1-3: inside `while (i < n)` inString is always false, because the carry block either closes the string or leaves i >= n, and case 0x22 either closes the string or sets inString = true only with i >= n.

Replace `case 0x22: // "  inString = true; lineHasContent = true; break;` (L304-307) with an in-place scanner that ends in `continue` so the switch-trailing `i++` (L344) is skipped: `case 0x22: { lineHasContent = true; i++; /* step over the opening quote */ for (;;) { while (i + 3 < n && buf[i] > 0x5c && buf[i + 1] > 0x5c && buf[i + 2] > 0x5c && buf[i + 3] > 0x5c) i += 4; if (i >= n) { inString = true; /* string still open at chunk end */ break; } const sb = buf[i++]; if (sb > 0x5c) continue; if (sb === 0x22) break; /* closing quote; i is already past it */ if (sb === 0x5c) { if (i < n) { i++; /* skip escaped byte */ } else { inString = true; escaped = true; /* escape straddles the chunk boundary */ break; } } /* other bytes <= 0x5c, including raw newlines inside strings, change no state */ } continue; }`. The braces scope `const sb` (no-case-declarations). A quote as the last byte of a chunk gives i === n, sets inString = true, and the carry block in the next chunk takes over. A backslash as the last byte sets inString = true and escaped = true with i === n, exactly the state the old code left. Raw newlines in strings are still skipped without counting a line, as before.

Leave everything else byte-for-byte unchanged: the module-level WCLS table, the WCLS skip, cases 0x7b/0x5b/0x7d/0x5d, case 0x0a (including its `if (depth === 0 && !inString)` test, which is now always true for inString but stays as is to keep the change minimal), the default case, `i++` after the switch, `totalBytes += n;`, onProgress, the EOF block (`if (startOff < totalBytes) { ... if (depth > 0 || inString) sawMultiline = true; ... } else if (depth > 0 || inString) { ... }`), and the records/endsWithNewline construction. Do NOT add a Uint32Array view, SWAR haszero word loop, alignment gate, indexOf skipping or class table inside strings, and do NOT change the 4x reject. Run `npx prettier --write src/indexer/lineIndex.ts` so formatting matches the repo style. Confirm with `git diff --stat` that only src/indexer/lineIndex.ts changed and `git diff --quiet -- scripts/benchmark-index-build.mjs` exits 0.

expected_outcome.estimated_impact: +8-10% relative (sealed ~1.75-1.80 from best 1.623; today's base measures 1.60-1.68 on this machine)
expected_outcome.rationale: Round-5 scratch isolation of exactly this shape (r5/src/indexer/quoteInline.ts, generated from base.ts = 1d2377e) measured in-process paired rel median 1.159 (q1 0.994, q3 1.319) and sealed-benchmark copies at 1.787/1.790 against base 1.605/1.640 in the same sweep, and it passed all 576 differential cases, including chunk-straddling strings and a trailing backslash at a chunk end. The gain comes from control flow, not per-byte work: about 75% of fixture bytes sit in strings of ~26 B, so the per-string round trip through the outer loop (inString/escaped re-tests, extra i++ and loop-condition checks) and the per-outside-byte `if (inString)` test are a real share of cost after the round-2 string loop and round-3 WCLS skip. It differs from round-1 quoteFirst/quoteDirect peeling (neutral), which only reordered the switch dispatch while keeping the top-of-loop inString branch, and from strHoist (neutral, rel 1.033), which only moved the `if (escaped)` test. Honest outlook: it will probably land just under the 1.8 target on its own. It is the second-family plan, orthogonal to planner_a's swarRG word loop, and could stack with it in a later round.

The round-4 360a642 shape (word loop in front of a kept 4x reject, 1.590). The round-1 sync scanChunk kernel / ScanState marshaling (0.897) and index-based array iteration (0.882). Buffer#indexOf quote/newline skipping (slower on short strings, wrong for raw newlines in strings). Class table inside strings. nextCp counter, lazy recordEndLines and Float64Array offsets (neutral/negative). quoteFirst/quoteDirect peeling, viewU8, skipDef, rej4n3 (neutral). DataView or 2-word SWAR (negative). strHoist (neutral). Stacking quoteInline with swarRG is left to a later round (two changes).
